In [[geometry]], the '''great hexacronic icositetrahedron''' is the dual of the [[great cubicuboctahedron]]. Its faces are [[Kite (geometry)|kites]]. Part of each kite lies inside the solid, hence is invisible in solid models.

== Proportions==
The kites have two angles of <math>\arccos(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{2})\approx 117.200\,570\,380\,16^{\circ}</math>, one of <math>\arccos(-\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{8}\sqrt{2})\approx 94.199\,144\,429\,76^{\circ}</math> and one of <math>\arccos(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{2})\approx 31.399\,714\,809\,92^{\circ}</math>. The [[dihedral angle]] equals <math>\arccos(\frac{-7+4\sqrt{2}}{17})\approx 94.531\,580\,798\,20^{\circ}</math>. The ratio between the lengths of the long and short edges is <math>2+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{2}\approx 2.70710678118655</math>.
